Insert:
The Comptroller-General of Customs may establish controlled trials. A controlled trial is for a period of up to 12 months, with a possible one-off extension of up to 6 months.
Entities may apply or be invited to participate in a controlled trial.
Entities participating in a controlled trial:
may be released from certain obligations under this Act; or
may be required to satisfy certain obligations under this Act in a different way to that required by this Act; or
may be required to comply with additional obligations; or
may receive benefits of a certain kind.
This Part applies in relation to the following entities:
individuals;
bodies corporate;
partnerships.

division.heading: Obligations and benefits under controlled trials

content.p: Entities released from obligations

If an entity holds an approval, that is in force, to participate in a controlled trial, the entity is released from an obligation that the entity would otherwise be required to satisfy under a controlled trial provision if the obligation is specified in the rules as an obligation in relation to that trial that entities are released from.
Note 1: Section 179L provides for the making of rules to establish a controlled trial. Division 3 deals with approving an entity’s participation in a controlled trial.
Note 2: For controlled trial provision, see subsection 4(1).
Entities must satisfy obligations in a different way

If an entity holds an approval, that is in force, to participate in a controlled trial, the entity cannot satisfy an obligation under a controlled trial provision in the way required by this Act if the obligation is specified in the rules as an obligation in relation to that trial that entities cannot satisfy in the way required by this Act.
Instead, the entity must satisfy the obligation in the way specified in the rules in relation to that trial.
Note: A failure to satisfy the obligation in this way is a ground for varying, suspending or revoking the entity’s approval: see section 179J.
Entities must comply with additional obligations

If an entity holds an approval, that is in force, to participate in a controlled trial, the entity must comply with each obligation specified in the rules as an obligation in relation to that trial that entities must comply with.
Note 1: The obligation must be in relation to a controlled trial provision: see paragraph 179L(3)(h).
Note 2: A failure to comply with the obligation is a ground for varying, suspending or revoking the entity’s approval: see section 179J.
If an entity holds an approval, that is in force, to participate in a controlled trial, the entity may receive benefits of a kind that are specified in the rules in relation to the trial.

section.heading: Approval of participation in controlled trials

content.p: The Comptroller-General of Customs may, in writing, approve an entity’s participation in a controlled trial if:
either:
the entity makes an application to participate in that trial in accordance with section 179F; or
the Comptroller-General of Customs invites, in writing, the entity to participate in that trial and the entity makes an election to participate in that trial in accordance with section 179G; and
the Comptroller-General of Customs is satisfied that the entity meets the qualification criteria (if any) determined in an instrument under section 179K; and
the Comptroller-General of Customs is satisfied that the entity meets the eligibility criteria (if any) specified in the rules in relation to that trial.
Note: Section 179F deals with making applications and section 179G deals with making elections.
In deciding whether to approve an entity’s participation in a controlled trial, the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider:
any matter specified in the rules under paragraph 179L(3)(b) in relation to that trial; and
any other matter that the Comptroller-General of Customs considers relevant.
Period for which approval is in force
An approval under subsection (1) must specify the period for which it is in force.
Note: See section 179J for variation, suspension or revocation of an approval.
Copy of approval to be given to entity
The Comptroller-General of Customs must give a copy of an approval under subsection (1) to the entity.
Notification of refusal to approve entity’s participation in controlled trial

If an entity makes an application or election to participate in a controlled trial and the Comptroller-General of Customs refuses to approve the entity’s participation in the trial, the Comptroller-General of Customs must notify the entity of the refusal and of the reasons for the refusal.
Approval not a legislative instrument
An approval under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Application to participate in controlled trial

content.p: An application to participate in a controlled trial may be made by document or electronically.
Documentary application
A documentary application must:
be communicated to the Comptroller-General of Customs; and
be in an approved form; and
contain the information required by the approved form; and
be signed in a manner indicated by the approved form.
Electronic application
An electronic application must:
be communicated to the Comptroller-General of Customs; and
communicate such information as is set out in an approved statement.

section.heading: Election to participate in controlled trial

content.p: An election to participate in a controlled trial may be made by document or electronically.
Documentary election
A documentary election must:
be communicated to the Comptroller-General of Customs; and
be in an approved form; and
contain the information required by the approved form; and
be signed in a manner indicated by the approved form.
Electronic election
An electronic election must:
be communicated to the Comptroller-General of Customs; and
communicate such information as is set out in an approved statement.
An entity’s approval under section 179E in relation to a controlled trial is subject to the conditions specified in the rules in relation to that trial.

section.heading: Variation, suspension or revocation of approvals

content.p: The Comptroller-General of Customs may, in writing, vary, suspend or revoke an entity’s approval under section 179E in relation to a controlled trial if the Comptroller-General of Customs is satisfied that:
the entity no longer meets the qualification criteria (if any) determined in an instrument under section 179K; or
the entity no longer meets the eligibility criteria (if any) specified in the rules in relation to that trial; or
the entity has not complied, or is not complying, with any condition specified in the rules in relation to that trial; or
in relation to that trial, the entity has not satisfied an obligation covered by subsection 179C(2) in the way covered by subsection 179C(3); or
in relation to that trial, the entity has not complied with an obligation covered by subsection 179C(4).
In deciding whether to vary, suspend or revoke an approval, the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider:
any matter specified in the rules under paragraph 179L(3)(d) in relation to that trial; and
any other matter that the Comptroller-General of Customs considers relevant.
A variation, suspension or revocation of an approval must be in accordance with the procedures specified in the rules in relation to that trial.
The Comptroller-General of Customs must give notice of a variation, suspension or revocation to the entity.
The notice must specify the day the variation, suspension or revocation takes effect (which must be at least 7 days after the day the notice is given).
Consequences of suspension
An approval has no effect while suspended, but the period for which it remains in force continues to run despite the suspension.
The Comptroller-General of Customs may, in writing, revoke a suspension under subsection (1).
The Comptroller-General of Customs must give notice of the revocation of the suspension to the entity. The notice must specify the day the revocation takes effect.
The Comptroller-General of Customs may, under subsection (1), vary or revoke an approval while it is suspended.

section.heading: General qualification criteria for any controlled trial

content.p: The Comptroller-General of Customs may, by legislative instrument, determine qualification criteria that entities must meet in order to participate in any controlled trial.

section.heading: Rules specific to a controlled trial

content.p: The Comptroller-General of Customs may, by legislative instrument, make rules that make provision for and in relation to the following:
establishing a controlled trial;
the period of operation of a controlled trial;
extending the period of operation of a controlled trial;
revoking a controlled trial.
For the purposes of subsection (1):
rules that establish a controlled trial must specify the purpose of the controlled trial; and
the period of operation of a controlled trial must not be more than 12 months; and
the period of operation of a controlled trial may begin after the day on which the controlled trial is established; and
an extension of the period of operation of a controlled trial must not be more than 6 months; and
the period of operation of a controlled trial must not be extended more than once.
The Comptroller-General of Customs may, by legislative instrument, make rules that make provision for and in relation to the following for a controlled trial:
the eligibility criteria that an entity must meet in order for the Comptroller-General of Customs to approve an entity’s participation in that trial;
the matters that the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider in deciding whether to approve an entity’s participation in that trial;
the conditions that approvals under section 179E in relation to that trial are subject to;
the matters that the Comptroller-General of Customs must consider when deciding whether to vary, suspend or revoke an approval under section 179E in relation to that trial;
the procedures that the Comptroller-General of Customs must follow when varying, suspending or revoking an approval under section 179E in relation to that trial;
each obligation under a controlled trial provision that, in relation to that trial, entities holding an approval, that is in force, to participate in that trial are released from;
the following:

each obligation under a controlled trial provision that, in relation to that trial, entities holding an approval, that is in force, to participate in that trial cannot satisfy in the way required by this Act;
the way in which those entities must satisfy that obligation;

each obligation that, in relation to that trial, entities holding an approval, that is in force, to participate in that trial must comply with, being an obligation that is in relation to a controlled trial provision;
the kind of benefits that entities holding an approval, that is in force, to participate in that trial may receive and any criteria to be satisfied for entities to receive those benefits;
a matter that is incidental or ancillary to a matter covered by paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g), (h) or (i).
Note: For controlled trial provision, see subsection 4(1).
To avoid doubt, rules made under this section may not do the following:
create an offence or civil penalty;
provide powers of:
arrest or detention; or
entry, search or seizure;
impose a tax;
set an amount to be appropriated from the Consolidated Revenue Fund under an appropriation in this Act;
directly amend the text of this Act.
